messages.content: You are the neutral rapporteur of a technology readiness review panel. Consolidate, attribute and preserve disagreement; do not decide and do not add technical claims of your own.

# Synthesis: assess · T02

## Claude Opus 5.5


# TRL assessment: T02, MW-scale deployable solar arrays (cargo tug, plus NEA site power per Gemini and GPT)

## Assessment basis and assumptions

**Required, sized at the maximum operating distance.** I follow the Claude/GPT position: size at the maximum heliocentric distance of the operating envelope, not at a fixed 1.2 AU. Neither the target list nor the maximum tug range is fixed yet, so I bracket them.

| Case | EOL requirement | Max distance (assumed) | EOL degradation (assumed) | BOL equivalent at 1 AU | Area at ~330 W/m² (1 AU BOL, III-V, ~85% packing) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tug, low | 1.0 MWe | 1.3 AU | 20% | ~2.1 MW | ~6,400 m² |
| Tug, high | 2.5 MWe | 1.7 AU | 20% | ~9.0 MW | ~27,000 m² |
| Site, low | 2.5 MW | 1.3 AU (NEA aphelion) | 20% | ~5.3 MW | ~16,000 m² |
| Site, high | 8 MW | 1.3 AU | 20% | ~17 MW | ~51,000 m² |

- The 20% degradation over 10–15 yr is an assumption. It covers interplanetary proton fluence, UV, thermal cycling and contamination. It is not a validated figure (see the rq-0-25 caveats below).
- The low-intensity, low-temperature efficiency gain at 1.3–1.7 AU gives perhaps 5–10% credit. I have not taken it.
- Fleet total: 10–18 tugs plus the site comes to roughly **30–180 MW of 1 AU-BOL array**. That is a supply-chain fact as much as a technology fact.

**Thrust load (dynamics under thrust).** F ≈ 2ηP/(g₀·Isp). With η ≈ 0.6:

- 1 MWe at 3,000 s gives ≈ 40 N.
- 2.5 MWe at 2,000 s gives ≈ 150 N.

Quasi-static acceleration is small (~10⁻⁴ m/s² on a 300–500 t stack). The concern is the dynamics, not strength:

- Very low fundamental frequencies in 6,000–27,000 m² flexible structures.
- Coupling with attitude control, gimbal slews and thrust vectoring.
- Thermal snap at eclipse and shadow transitions.
- Throttling transients.

My assumption is wing fundamentals of order 0.01–0.1 Hz at this scale. That is not verified.

**What I am rating.** I rate the integrated array system at MW scale, not the cell or the individual heritage wing. The two elements (tug and site) are rated separately because their environments differ:

- Tug: thrust dynamics and plume contamination.
- Site: charged NEA dust, low gravity or free-flying station-keeping, and 1–3 kV tether distribution.

## 1. Evidence

| Heritage | Year | Demonstrated | Ratio to required (BOL 1 AU equiv.) | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ISS Photovoltaic Arrays (8 Si wings, ~2,500 m² total, ~31 kW-class per wing), crew-assembled over ~9 yr | 2000–2009 | ~100–240 kW total gross at 1 AU, LEO | Tug 9–90×; site 22–170× (by power). Area: tug 2.5–11×, site 6–20× ISS | Confident on programme and area. Per-wing and total power figures approximate |
| iROSA roll-out arrays on ISS (Redwire), ~20+ kW each | 2021–2023 | ~20–30 kW per wing, LEO, robotic and EVA install | Per wing: ~70–450× | Confident on programme. Per-wing power approximate |
| ROSA flight experiment on ISS | 2017 | Subscale deployment and retraction, dynamics data | >1,000× | Confident it flew. Power not stated here |
| DART (ROSA wings, interplanetary to ~1.1 AU) | 2021–2022 | Low single-digit to ~tens of kW | >100× | Confident ROSA flew on DART. Power figure unsure |
| Psyche (Maxar, SEP, to ~3.3 AU) | 2023– | ~20 kW-class at 1 AU, flexible-rigid hybrid, deep-space SEP | ~100–450× | Moderately confident (~21 kW at 1 AU) |
| Lucy (UltraFlex, ~7 m wings) | 2021– | ~18 kW-class at 1 AU. One wing did not latch fully, a relevant deployment-anomaly datum | ~100–500× | Confident on the latching anomaly. Power approximate |
| Dawn, Juno, Rosetta | 2007–2016+ | ~10–14 kW-class at 1 AU, III-V or Si, multi-year outside the magnetosphere | ~150–900× | Confident these flew outside the magnetosphere. Specific kW unsure |
| NASA Solar Array Systems (SAS) for SEP: ATK MegaFlex and DSS ROSA ground demos | ~2012–2015 | Wing-scale ground deployment of architectures claimed scalable to ~250 kW+ class. Not flown at that scale | ~10–40× vs claimed scalability; much more vs the tested hardware | Moderately confident on the programme. Unsure of test power and scale |
| Deep Space 1 SCARLET linear Fresnel concentrator | 1998 | ~2.5 kW, interplanetary | ~1,000× | Confident. Relevant only to the rq-0-22 concentrator branch |
| ThrustMe NPT30-I2 iodine gridded ion thruster in orbit (Rafalskyi et al., Nature 2021) | 2020 | Tens-of-W iodine EP flight | Contamination data at MW plume flux: none | Confident it flew. No array-contamination dataset I know of |
| High-voltage array operation | — | ISS ~160 V is the high-voltage heritage I am confident of. Higher voltages (≥300 V) exist in ground and small flight experiments | 1–3 kV array or direct-drive: ≥6–20× flight voltage | Confident on ISS. Unsure of the specific high-voltage flight experiments, so none cited |
| NASA Armstrong Test Facility Space Power Facility (~30 m × 37 m vacuum chamber) | Exists | Largest ground vacuum volume. Cannot host a MW array | Constrains the path | Confident |

**Cautions on the related RQ literature.** These RQs are written for the superseded 100 MW L4/L5 architecture. They are partly useful for cells and degradation, but they are not evidence at TRL ≥3 for this system.

- **rq-0-22: cell cost.** It cites III-V cell cost of "$100–300/cm²". That implies ~$1–3 M/m², which looks wrong by orders of magnitude. Do not propagate.
- **rq-0-22: concentrator waste heat.** It cites "~350 W/cm² waste heat at 500×". 500 × 0.136 W/cm² is ~68 W/cm² incident, so waste heat is ~45 W/cm². The number is wrong.
- **rq-0-22: concentrator heritage.** It lists "ISS solar arrays" as concentrator heritage. They are flat-plate Si.
- **rq-0-22 vs rq-0-25: annealing temperature.** They disagree on the Lang et al. temperature: 60 °C under AM0 versus 100–200 °C. Lang et al. is on GaInAsP, not the InGaP/GaAs/Ge baseline. Annealing credit is unvalidated.
- **rq-0-25: degradation rate.** The 1.0–1.7%/yr estimate is a synthesis, not a test result.
- **rq-0-25: STEREO.** The claim that STEREO used silicon arrays is unverified by me.
- **rq-0-25: remaining factor.** The specific value "0.85–0.90 at 10¹⁰ MeV/g" is likewise unverified.
- **Use with care.** The arXiv NIEL/DDD papers (Baur, Campesato et al.) are appropriate underlying physics for cell degradation, i.e. TRL 1–3 evidence at cell level.

## 2. Current TRL

**Tug array: TRL 3, upper bound 4.**

- **Met at TRL 3:** Key parameters are validated experimentally in pieces:
  - Flexible-blanket specific power and deployment at the 20–30 kW wing scale (flight).
  - III-V degradation versus displacement damage dose (ground irradiation plus deep-space flight).
  - SEP array operation in deep space (Psyche, Dawn).
- **Why the upper bound is 4:** TRL 4 is reachable only if one accepts "N × heritage wings" as the breadboard.
- **Unmet for TRL 4:**
  - No documented definition of the relevant environment. Propellant is unselected (iodine vs argon plume), maximum distance is unfixed, and there are no thrust and slew load spectra. This is part of the TRL 4 exit criterion itself.
  - No laboratory breadboard whose performance has been checked against predictions for the MW-scale emergent functions:
    - multi-wing structural dynamics under thrust;
    - harness and high-voltage (≥300 V, plausibly up to kV) plasma interaction and arcing;
    - iodine deposition and corrosion on coverglass, interconnects and slip rings;
    - hinge/mast scaling beyond the heritage ratio.

**Site array: TRL 2, upper bound 3.**

- **Met at TRL 2:** Concept documented (Gemini/GPT). It is static and unthrusted, which is easier than the tug.
- **Unmet for TRL 3:** No experimental data on:
  - charged regolith dust adhesion and obscuration rates for NEA-like conditions near active excavation (tailings 13–47 kt/yr);
  - anchoring or station-keeping of tens of thousands of m² at a rotating milligravity body;
  - 1–3 kV distribution from array to tether.

The governing range is reported as 2–4.

## 3. Target and difficulty

**Target: TRL 6 at KDP-0B.** Tug and site power is the dominant input to delivered $/kg. Under D-02 the economics gate cannot be credibly passed on a TRL 3 power system. I recommend TRL 6 even though I classify failure as architecture-change rather than project-ending (see §5).

- TRL 6 must be met with a subscale prototype (≥100–300 kW-class, multi-wing) in a relevant environment, plus a validated scaling model.
  - A full-scale MW ground test is physically impossible; even the Space Power Facility is far too small.
  - In practice this means a flight demonstration on the 0A pathfinder, or a dedicated flight.
  - Ground vacuum, thermal and plume tests can reach TRL 5 at most.
- **Internal 0A milestone:** TRL 4 by the 0A mid-term review, TRL 5 before pathfinder CDR.
- **Needed by:** KDP-0B. The date is not set; I assume ~2031–2034.
- **Phase tag:** 0B. 0A scouts at 200–600 kg use existing kW arrays and do not need T02.

**AD² = 5 (range 5–6).**

- This is new development. Nothing similar has been done: no autonomously deployed array has exceeded ~0.1 MW.
- The flat-plate flexible-blanket path is reasonably clear: scaling ROSA/MegaFlex-type wings and multi-wing modular masts.
- Arguments for 6:
  - Competing approaches remain unresolved: number and size of wings, robotic in-space assembly vs one-shot deployment, high-voltage direct drive vs low voltage plus PPU, flat-plate vs concentrator (rq-0-22).
  - Iodine compatibility could force design changes.
  - Robotic assembly heritage is thin. OSAM-1 was cancelled, and Caltech SSPD-1/DOLCE (2023) was a small-scale deployment with partial issues.

## 4. Path

| # | Step | Method | Scale | Cost (USD) | Duration | Reaches |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Relevant-environment definition: max distance, SEP/proton fluence (SPENVIS/OMERE-class models), iodine and argon plume backflow models, thrust/slew load spectra, NEA dust environment | analysis | System | 0.5–2 M | 0.5–1 yr | Prerequisite for 4 |
| 2 | Cell plus coverglass irradiation to interplanetary 10–15 yr proton/electron spectra, 2–3 coverglass thicknesses, with UV | experiment | Coupons, cells | 0.5–3 M | 1–2 yr | Cell-level 5 |
| 3 | Iodine (and argon) exposure of coverglass, interconnects, hinges, slip rings; corrosion and transmission loss; also dust adhesion with charged NEA simulant | experiment | Coupons, small panels | 1–6 M | 1–2 yr | 4 |
| 4 | High-voltage (300 V–1+ kV) plasma-interaction and arcing tests on string segments in a plasma chamber | experiment | String/panel | 2–10 M | 1–2 yr | 4–5 |
| 5 | Multi-wing structural-dynamics model with control and thrust coupling, validated against existing ROSA/iROSA flight dynamics data | simulation | MW configurations | 2–8 M | 1–2 yr | 4 (with steps 1–4) |
| 6 | Wing-level (≥100–250 kW-class) ground deployment, thermal-vacuum on segments, gravity-offload dynamics | experiment | 1 wing (~1/10–1/40 of tug) | 30–120 M | 2–4 yr | 5 |
| 7 | Flight demo: ≥200–500 kW multi-wing array on the 0A pathfinder, operated with EP at thrust, ≥1–2 yr, with the selected propellant | experiment | ~1/5–1/40 of tug | 150–500 M (excl. launch) | 3–6 yr incl. ops | 6, arguably 7 |
| 8 | Site-specific: dust and anchoring or station-keeping demo at a scout target, small array coupon near surface operations | experiment | Coupon/kW | 5–30 M (as scout payload) | 2–4 yr | Site 4–5 |
| 9 | Supply-chain analysis: space-grade III-V output versus a fleet need of 30–180 MW; alternatives such as Si heterojunction or thin-film with lower EOL performance | analysis | Programme | 0.2–1 M | 0.5 yr | n/a, gates feasibility |

On step 9, I am unsure of current world space III-V output. I believe it is far below tens of MW/yr; please verify.

## 5. Risk and fallback

**Risk class: architecture-change.** It becomes project-ending only if combined with an economics-gate failure. Without MW arrays, 0B can still fall back to:

- more tugs at ~0.3–0.6 MWe, with longer trips and a larger fleet;
- lower site power with reduced throughput, which the 0.6–2.5 kt/yr Fe-Ni product may tolerate;
- or nuclear fission power, which is lower TRL at MW scale and is not a near-term fallback.

These degrade delivered $/kg, so failure can cascade to a D-02 economics failure. That cascade ends in the pre-committed "0A only, Earth supply" outcome.

**Fallback:** Re-baseline tugs to the largest flight-demonstrated array (~0.3–0.5 MWe class modular wings) with fleet count and trip time increased. Site power drops to the demonstrated level, and the economics gate is re-run.

## 6. Where others might disagree

1. **"It is just N heritage wings" (likely Gemini/GPT optimism).** On this view the system is TRL 5–6 because each wing is TRL 9 at 20–30 kW. I reject it. TRL is rated at the required scale, and the critical functions are emergent at MW scale: dynamics under thrust, high-voltage plasma interaction, iodine contamination, harness mass, and 70–450× wing count or size scaling. Integrating 100+ heritage wings on one tug is itself untested.
2. **Risk class.** A reviewer could argue project-ending: without ≥1 MWe tugs the delivered-cost model may never close. I keep architecture-change because degraded fallbacks exist, but the gap to project-ending is narrow.
3. **Site TRL may be underrated.** A static site array without thrust loads is simpler. The counterargument is that dust from 13–47 kt/yr of tailings handling and milligravity anchoring have no data at all.
4. **Sizing distance.** Fixing 1.2 AU instead of the maximum distance would cut tug area by ~2× and make the problem look easier. I follow Claude/GPT, but the factor matters to the scale ratio.
5. **Degradation and annealing credit.** The RQ literature implies 0.8–1.7%/yr with annealing credit. I treat this as unvalidated. Annealing evidence is on GaInAsP, and the two RQs give inconsistent temperatures.
6. **Concentrators.** rq-0-22's concentrator case rests partly on erroneous numbers. SCARLET is the only relevant space heritage, at ~2.5 kW. I do not rate a CPV branch.

## Gemini 3.1 Pro


### 1. Evidence

The requirement is for 1–2.5 MWe deployable solar arrays per tug, operating under electric propulsion thrust dynamics, exposed to deep-space radiation, potential iodine propellant plume contamination, and mining dust, with a 10–15 year life. 

- **Current flight heritage:** The ISS Roll-Out Solar Array (iROSA) and the Gateway Power and Propulsion Element (PPE) arrays represent the state of the art for high-power deployable arrays. The PPE arrays (Maxar/Deployable Space Systems) are designed for ~50 kW per wing (TRL 6-8 for Gateway). 
- **Scale ratio:** The required 1–2.5 MWe per tug is 20× to 50× larger than the largest currently flown or qualified single array systems.
- **Environment:** Deep space radiation for III-V cells is well understood (TRL 8-9), but the combined effects of MW-scale structural dynamics under continuous low-thrust, iodine plume backflow (iodine is highly reactive with many spacecraft materials), and abrasive NEA dust on array surfaces at this scale have only been modeled or tested at component levels. Iodine plume interaction with solar cells has been tested in small vacuum chambers (e.g., ThrustMe NPT30-I2, 2021), but not at the MW scale where plasma sheath effects differ.

### 2. Current TRL

**TRL 3–4.** 
- **Lower bound met (TRL 3):** Analytical and experimental proof of concept exists for the underlying technologies (flexible blanket arrays, III-V cells, iodine plume interactions at small scale).
- **Unmet exit criterion (TRL 4/5):** Component and/or breadboard validation in a laboratory environment of the deployment mechanisms, structural dynamics under thrust, and iodine/dust mitigation strategies at the MW scale. No documented test performance of a MW-class array structure exists.

### 3. Target and difficulty

- **Target:** TRL 6 by KDP-0B (project-ending for the tug architecture if power cannot be generated). Needed by 2029 for Phase 0B procurement.
- **AD²: 5.** New development; similar development has not been done (MW-scale space arrays), but the path is clear (scaling up ROSA-style or folded-panel architectures, though structural dynamics at this scale are non-trivial).

### 4. Path

1. **Plume & Dust Interaction Testing:** Laboratory vacuum testing of III-V cell coupons and coverglasses exposed to iodine plasma and simulated NEA dust to validate degradation models. (TRL 4, $2M–$5M, 1–2 years).
2. **Sub-scale Structural Dynamics:** Ground testing of a ~100–250 kW class array wing to validate deployment kinematics and structural stiffness models under simulated thrust loads. (TRL 5, $15M–$30M, 2–3 years).
3. **System Prototype Demonstration:** Thermal-vacuum deployment and structural testing of a full-scale (or half-scale, 500 kW) array quadrant, combined with high-fidelity simulations of the full 1–2.5 MW system. (TRL 6, $50M–$100M, 3–4 years).

### 5. Risk and fallback

- **Risk if fail:** Architecture-change. If MW-scale arrays cannot be deployed or stabilized, the architecture must fall back to multiple smaller tugs (e.g., 200–500 kW each), drastically increasing the number of vehicles, or shift to nuclear electric propulsion (which has its own severe TRL and regulatory hurdles).
- **Fallback:** Scale down tugs to 300–500 kWe using multiple Gateway-class arrays, increasing fleet size and mission complexity.

### 6. Where others might disagree

Some might argue that because solar panels are highly modular, scaling from 50 kW to 2.5 MW is merely an engineering exercise (TRL 5). However, the structural dynamics of a multi-megawatt array under continuous thrust, combined with the specific environmental hazards of iodine and dust, introduce fundamental non-linearities that invalidate simple scaling assumptions.

## GPT-6.1 Sol


## T02 — MW-scale deployable solar arrays

**Assessment: current TRL 2–3 for the architecture-required subsystem; target TRL 6 at KDP-0B; AD² 5.** Flight-proven photovoltaic cells and deployable arrays provide substantial heritage, but do **not** establish readiness of a 1–2.5 MWe tug array or a 2.5–8 MW asteroid-site installation with the specified lifetime, contamination exposure and structural dynamics.

The lower rating applies to the **integrated, architecture-specific technology**, not to solar cells or existing commercial array products.

### Assessment boundary and assumptions

- **Tugs:** 1–2.5 MWe **net usable EOL power**, including array-side conversion and distribution losses, at the maximum powered operating distance—or with explicitly accepted propulsion derating.
- **Sites:** 2.5–8 MW net usable EOL power. I assume an Earth-manufactured, modular flat-plate installation, rather than locally manufactured cells or structures.
- **Lifetime:** 10–15 years. Accelerated testing and validated life models can support TRL 6; a literal 15-year prototype flight is not required.
- **Environment:** vacuum, solar-particle radiation, operational temperature changes, deployment in microgravity, and applicable site anchoring or free-flying-array dynamics. Tug arrays must remain stable under thrust and attitude manoeuvres. Site arrays require protection against charged dust and processing contamination.
- **Distance:** 0.9–1.3 AU is the stated environmental envelope, **not evidence that every selected tug trajectory stays inside it**. Actual trajectory maxima must be established before design freeze.
- **Electrical boundary:** array strings, deployment structure, pointing, harnessing and array-side power conditioning are included. Complete site distribution and propulsion-system readiness are separate assessments, although their interfaces must be demonstrated.

The older **100 MW at SEL4/5, $500 million, 600 V** research framing is superseded. Its cost, module-size and degradation assumptions are not requirements or readiness evidence for the revised architecture.

## 1. Evidence

Ratios below are **required power ÷ demonstrated power**, not a claim that power alone determines scaling.

| Heritage | Physical evidence and environment | Demonstrated scale | Ratio to revised requirement | Limits on credit |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| **NASA Roll-Out Solar Array experiment, ISS, 2017** | A flexible roll-out array deployed in orbit; its structural response was measured during an ISS experiment. NASA’s *Roll-Out Solar Array* experiment reporting documents the deployment and dynamics investigation. | Approximately 1.6 × 6 m experimental wing; not a MW power demonstration. | Power ratio: **not applicable**. | Establishes relevant deployment and flexible-structure test heritage. The experiment did not establish MW-scale thrust-coupled dynamics or a 15-year life. Retraction was unsuccessful and the experiment was subsequently jettisoned; deployment success must not be reported as complete mechanism success. |
| **NASA ISS Roll-Out Solar Arrays, installation beginning 2021** | Operational roll-out photovoltaic arrays on ISS. NASA’s 2021 iROSA installation reporting states that each new array produces more than 20 kW. | Approximately **20 kW per wing**, nominal—not architecture-specific EOL power. | Tug: **50–125×**; site: **125–400×**, using 20 kW as the comparison baseline. | Strong evidence for modular blanket integration, deployment and operation. LEO, station support, pointing arrangements and loading differ from a free-flying electric tug or asteroid installation. |
| **NASA/JPL Psyche, launched 2023** | Large deployed solar arrays operating during interplanetary cruise. NASA/JPL’s 2023 mission and spacecraft descriptions report approximately 75 m² total array area and 21 kW near Earth. | Approximately **21 kW near 1 AU**; two deployed wings. | Tug: **48–119×**; site: **119–381×**. | Relevant deep-space photovoltaic/deployment heritage. The quoted power is not a demonstrated 15-year EOL rating, and Psyche does not validate MW electrical or structural scaling. |
| **NASA/JPL Deep Space 1 / SCARLET, 1998–2001** | A deployed solar concentrator array powered a deep-space electric-propulsion mission. NASA/JPL’s 1998 *Deep Space 1* press kit documents the approximately 2.5 kW array. | Approximately **2.5 kW near 1 AU**. | Tug: **400–1,000×**; site: **1,000–3,200×**. | Supports a **low-concentration** alternative, not the supplied 500× concentrator concept or MW-scale concentrator deployment. |

These programme claims are ones I am confident exist. The numerical ratios remain approximate because the heritage ratings and the required **net EOL** ratings are not identical measurement bases.

### What the supplied literature does—and does not—establish

I would not adopt the supplied literature reviews’ numerical fluences, annual degradation rates, confidence intervals or cost estimates without checking the underlying papers and calculations. In particular:

- Electron-irradiation results alone do not qualify a cell/coverglass assembly for the mission’s **proton spectrum and fluence**.
- Annealing observations in one semiconductor composition do not establish a recoverable power allowance for the selected flight cell.
- Sun–Earth L4/L5 do **not** experience routine Earth eclipses as described in the supplied review.
- ISS iROSA is **not concentrator-array heritage**.
- High-concentration systems reduce **cell area**, not the collection aperture needed to intercept sunlight. Their optics, heat spreading, pointing and degradation remain separate scaling problems.
- Flat-plate cell heat is largely rejected directly from the array surfaces; it should not automatically be assigned to the plant’s process-radiator budget.

The supplied arXiv references may contain useful component evidence, but I have not independently verified their bibliographic details and quoted results here. They receive no additional integrated-system TRL credit in this assessment.

## 2. Current TRL and unmet criteria

### Integrated flat-plate subsystem: **TRL 2–3**

**TRL 2 is met:** the application, functional concept and feasibility basis are documented, and closely related physical technologies exist.

**TRL 3 is the conditional upper bound:** existing deployment and structural-response experiments can support critical-function proof of concept **if** a documented, test-correlated scaling analysis shows that they validate key parameters of the proposed modular MW design. No such architecture-specific correlation package is supplied.

**The next exit criterion is unmet:**

- From the conservative **TRL 2** position: documented experimental or test-validated analytical results validating the proposed system’s key parameters.
- From the conditional **TRL 3** position: a component/breadboard laboratory demonstration with performance agreeing with predictions **and a documented relevant environment**.

Neither a design study nor multiplication of flight-proven 20 kW wings satisfies these criteria by itself.

### Keep the architectural disagreements separate

| Configuration | Current architecture-specific TRL | Main distinction |
|---|---:|---|
| **Modular flat-plate tug array, Claude/GPT sizing rule** | **2–3** | Requires maximum-distance EOL sizing or explicit derating, plus thrust-coupled dynamics and contamination qualification. |
| **Modular flat-plate site installation, Gemini/GPT** | **2–3** | Independent modules may limit structural scaling, but installation, anchoring, dust control and MW aggregation remain unvalidated. |
| **Low-concentration deployable alternative** | **2–3** | Deep Space 1 provides useful heritage, but no MW qualification. |
| **500× concentrator interpretation of the older research question** | **2** | No supplied physical evidence validates its proposed space thermal, optical and pointing configuration at the required scale. |

The aggregate rating refers to the **flat-plate reference route**, not an average across these alternatives. Metallurgy route selection affects site power availability and duty cycle, but does not itself raise array TRL.

### Distance and EOL sizing are material, not bookkeeping

An illustrative calculation—not qualification evidence—is:

\[
P_{\rm net,EOL}/A =
\frac{1361}{r^2}\,
\eta_{\rm cell}\,f_{\rm packing}\,f_{\rm EOL}\,\eta_{\rm electrical}.
\]

Using explicitly assumed values of 0.30, 0.85, 0.80 and 0.95 respectively gives approximately **156 W/m² at 1.3 AU**:

- Tug active blanket footprint: approximately **6,400–16,000 m²**.
- Site active blanket footprint: approximately **16,000–51,000 m²**.

These exclude access gaps, deployment clearances, structural supports and reserve capacity. The assumed EOL factor is **not yet substantiated**.

Sizing at 1.3 rather than 1.2 AU requires about **17% more area**, all else equal. Beyond 1.3 AU, power must be resized or operational derating explicitly accepted. Radiation degradation should be expressed through mission-specific remaining-power factors and uncertainty bounds, not an unsupported constant annual percentage.

## 3. Target and difficulty

- **Internal 0A target:** TRL **4–5**, with completed relevant-environment definition and test-correlated deployment, dynamics, electrical and life models.
- **KDP-0B target:** TRL **6**, without waiver, for each configuration selected to enable production or product transport.
- **Needed by:** **KDP-0B, before committing to the production/tug architecture.** No calendar date for that gate is supplied.
- **Indicative development interval:** **6–10 years after sustained funding and requirement closure**, assuming overlapping work packages. This is not a committed schedule.
- **AD²: 5**, using the project’s anchors: the development path is identifiable, but a comparable integrated MW deployable system in this environment has not been demonstrated.

AD² could rise to **6** if the project retains a monolithic multi-MW wing, high-concentration optics, poorly bounded iodine exposure, or an unresolved asteroid deployment/anchoring concept. It could fall to **4** only after tests substantiate a highly modular architecture with independently controlled, fault-isolated wings.

## 4. Path to the target

Costs are **rough-order planning allowances in 2026 USD**, not vendor quotations. They cover the indicated work packages, not the production fleet. Package durations overlap; the costs should not be treated as a priced programme baseline.

| Step | Scale and discriminating work | Cost | Duration | TRL outcome |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| **Close requirements and correlate heritage models** | Full mission power envelope; selected trajectories; 10–15-year proton/electron environment; candidate module layouts; thrust histories; plume transport; site dust deposition. Correlate structural models with available physical array-test data. | **$1–4M** | **0.5–1.5 yr** | **3**, only where test data validate key parameters. Otherwise remains 2. |
| **Cell, blanket and insulation qualification breadboards** | Flight-like cell/coverglass/adhesive stacks and representative strings. Proton and electron irradiation; UV/vacuum thermal exposure; iodine deposition and material compatibility; charged dust abrasion/deposition; combined-stress sequences. Validate EOL-power and insulation models. | **$4–15M** | **1.5–3 yr** | **4–5** for the tested components, not the integrated array. |
| **Full-scale repeat-unit deployment and electrical testing** | Proposed **50–250 kW modules**, or the actual selected repeat unit. Full-size deployment hardware and harnessing; gravity-offloaded modal tests; vacuum tests of critical mechanisms; representative voltage and current; partial shading, arc initiation, faults and isolation. Include site interfaces up to the selected 1–3 kV distribution voltage. | **$20–80M** | **2–4 yr** | **4–5** for the repeat-unit subsystem, subject to environment fidelity. |
| **MW integrated ground validation** | **1–2.5 MW tug electrical architecture** and representative **2.5–8 MW site aggregation** using flight-like modules, source emulation and hardware-in-the-loop control. Validate deployment sequence, coupled thrust/attitude response, fault containment and scaling. Test full-scale critical spans, joints and support interfaces. | **$30–120M** | **2–4 yr** | **5**. Gravity offloading alone cannot close microgravity dynamics. |
| **Relevant-environment prototype demonstration** | **1–2.5 MW modular flight prototype**, selected so the largest critical deployment geometry is represented; electric-propulsion thrust/attitude excitation, thermal changes and measured I–V performance. Site qualification additionally needs representative installation/support and dust-exposure demonstrations. Combine these with validated accelerated-life results. | **$400M–1.5B** | **4–7 yr** | **6**, only after measured performance agrees with predictions and remaining scaling is experimentally justified. |

The flight allowance is deliberately broad: power level, launch configuration, demonstrator propulsion, orbit and deployment geometry are not yet selected.

**A 100 kW flight article does not automatically qualify a 2.5 MW wing.** Conversely, a full 8 MW site flight installation need not be mandatory if independent repeat units and all critical aggregation/support effects are demonstrated and their scaling is validated. The acceptance basis must be agreed before testing.

The 0A pathfinder’s power and mass must remain compatible with its mission. A separate MW demonstrator is likely necessary; it should not be silently inserted into the 200–600 kg scout class.

## 5. Risk and fallback

**Primary classification: project-ending for the selected solar-powered 0B architecture.** Failure to substantiate EOL power, deployment reliability or dynamic stability prevents a no-waiver TRL-6 decision.

Distinguish the failure modes:

- Failure of the **1–2.5 MW-per-tug architecture** could require smaller, more numerous tugs and revised delivery schedules: **architecture-change**.
- Failure of a particular large wing or concentrator concept could be addressed with smaller flat-plate modules: **architecture-change**, usually with cost and mass penalties.
- Failure to qualify any economically acceptable site/tug solar configuration by KDP-0B triggers the pre-committed fallback: **0A only, Earth supply**.

Replacement modules and power derating are possible mitigations, not free readiness credit. Their launch burden, maintenance method and effects on signed Phase 1 delivery demand must be included in the delivered-cost gate.

## 6. Where others might disagree

1. **TRL 2–3 versus 4–5.** An assessor may classify this as an enlargement of flight-proven arrays. My lower rating reflects the absence of architecture-specific test-correlated MW scaling, rather than doubt about photovoltaic conversion. A genuine modular breadboard programme could justify 4–5.
2. **What must be demonstrated at full scale.** Total MW power can sometimes be aggregated without a proportionate structural extrapolation. A monolithic wing cannot claim that advantage merely by electrically subdividing its blanket.
3. **Tug versus site difficulty.** Tugs face thrust-coupled dynamics and propulsion contamination; sites face dust, installation and support uncertainty. Neither is universally harder.
4. **AD² 5 versus 6.** This turns chiefly on modularity and requirement closure. The reference rating assumes conventional flat-plate cells and repeatable deployable modules—not 500× concentration.
5. **Lifetime evidence.** Qualification by accelerated exposure is legitimate, but only with validated degradation models, combined-stress testing and stated confidence bounds. It is not equivalent to assuming a heritage annual degradation rate.

# Consolidated rating: T02, MW-scale deployable solar arrays

**Scope as assessed by the panel**
- **Tug arrays:** 1–2.5 MWe EOL each.
- **NEA site installation:** 2.5–8 MW (site requirement per Gemini/GPT).
- **Life:** 10–15 years.
- **Environment:** interplanetary, with EP thrust dynamics, iodine/argon plume exposure, and charged NEA dust at the site.

## 1. Summary table

| | Claude Opus 5.5 | Gemini 3.1 Pro | GPT-6.1 Sol |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Current TRL** | Tug 3 (upper bound 4); site 2 (upper bound 3). Governing range **2–4** | **3–4** (tug and site not separated) | **2–3** (flat-plate reference). By configuration: tug 2–3, site 2–3, low-concentration 2–3, 500× concentrator 2 |
| **AD²** | 5 (range 5–6) | 5 | 5 (could rise to 6 or fall to 4, depending on modularity and requirement closure) |
| **Target** | TRL 6 at KDP-0B. Internal: TRL 4 at 0A mid-term, TRL 5 before pathfinder CDR | TRL 6 at KDP-0B | TRL 6 at KDP-0B, no waiver. Internal 0A target: TRL 4–5 |
| **Needed by** | KDP-0B, assumed ~2031–2034 | 2029 (no source given) | KDP-0B; date unspecified |
| **Risk if fail** | Architecture-change ("gap to project-ending is narrow") | Architecture-change in §5 and YAML. §3 text says "project-ending for the tug architecture" (internal inconsistency) | **Project-ending** for the selected solar 0B architecture. Sub-cases (smaller tugs, smaller modules) are architecture-change |
| **Years to target** | 6–10 | 4–6 | 6–10 (after sustained funding and requirement closure) |
| **Route to TRL 6** | Subscale flight demo (≥200–500 kW multi-wing) plus validated scaling model | Ground TVAC of a 500 kW–1 MW quadrant plus simulation | 1–2.5 MW modular flight prototype plus validated accelerated-life package |
| **Confidence** | Medium | Medium | Medium |

## 2. Where the panel agrees

- **Rating level.** The rating applies to the *integrated MW-scale system*, not to cells or individual heritage wings. All three reject "N × heritage wings" as sufficient for TRL 5–6.
- **Target.** TRL 6 at KDP-0B; phase need is 0B.
- **AD².** All three give a central value of 5. Claude and GPT both name 6 as plausible if architectural choices stay open.
- **Common risks.** Each model's treatment differs:

  | Risk | Claude | Gemini | GPT |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Structural dynamics under thrust | Named as emergent at MW scale | Named as emergent at MW scale | Named as emergent at MW scale |
  | Iodine plume compatibility | Named | Named | Named |
  | Charged NEA dust at the site | Named | Named | Named |
  | High-voltage plasma interaction and arcing | Explicit | Not addressed | Explicit, as part of electrical fault and isolation testing |

- **Fallback.** All three fall back to smaller, more numerous tugs:
  - Claude: ~0.3–0.5 MWe.
  - Gemini: 300–500 kWe.
  - GPT: smaller modular flat-plate arrays with derating.
  - Claude and GPT both end the fallback chain at the pre-committed "0A only, Earth supply" outcome.
- **Old RQ material (rq-0-22, rq-0-25).** Claude and GPT agree that:
  - its 100 MW L4/L5 framing is superseded;
  - its degradation rates and annealing credit are unvalidated;
  - ISS arrays are not concentrator heritage.

  Gemini does not engage with the RQ material.
- **0A scouts.** Claude and GPT agree the 200–600 kg 0A scouts do not need or validate T02.

## 3. Where the panel diverges, and why

### 3.1 Current TRL: GPT 2–3, Claude 2–4, Gemini 3–4

**What each model relies on:**
- **Claude** credits TRL 3 for the tug on piecewise validation. Its evidence is flight blankets at 20–30 kW, III-V degradation versus displacement damage dose, and deep-space SEP operation. It caps the site at 2 because there is no dust, anchoring or kV data.
- **Gemini** credits TRL 3 on component-level proof of concept. Its evidence includes 50 kW Gateway PPE arrays and ThrustMe iodine work.
- **GPT** makes TRL 3 *conditional*. It requires a documented, test-correlated scaling analysis linking heritage experiments to the proposed modular MW design, and states that none is supplied.

**Unmet exit criterion.** All three agree that TRL 4 needs:
- a documented relevant environment; and
- a breadboard whose performance agrees with predictions.

**What would settle it.** A panel review of whether any existing document correlates ROSA/iROSA/Psyche test data with a candidate MW module layout, which is GPT's criterion. Producing that document is step 1 in both Claude's and GPT's paths. If it exists and holds up, TRL 3 is supportable for the tug. If not, GPT's TRL 2 floor stands.

### 3.2 Can TRL 6 be reached on the ground?

**Positions:**
- **Gemini** reaches TRL 6 with ground TVAC of a full or half-scale (500 kW) quadrant plus high-fidelity simulation.
- **Claude** says ground vacuum, thermal and plume tests reach TRL 5 at most. Its reasons:
  - a full-scale MW ground test is physically impossible;
  - the Space Power Facility (~30 × 37 m), which Claude cites alone, cannot host it.
- **GPT** says gravity offloading alone cannot close microgravity dynamics, so TRL 6 needs a flight prototype.

**What would settle it.** Two things:
1. Agree the TRL 6 acceptance basis before testing, as GPT recommends.
2. Compare gravity-offloaded ground modal results against on-orbit modal data for the same hardware (e.g. ROSA/iROSA flight dynamics data, which Claude proposes in its step 5). That comparison shows whether ground-correlated models can be trusted at larger scale.

### 3.3 Flight-demo scale and vehicle

**Positions:**
- **Claude:** ≥200–500 kW multi-wing demo (~1/5–1/40 of a tug) on "the 0A pathfinder", at $150–500M.
- **GPT:** 1–2.5 MW modular flight prototype at $400M–1.5B. GPT warns it "should not be silently inserted into the 200–600 kg scout class" and expects a separate demonstrator to be needed. GPT also says a full 8 MW site flight need not be mandatory if repeat units and aggregation effects are validated.

Claude's own text says 0A scouts at 200–600 kg use existing kW arrays. It is therefore unclear whether Claude's "0A pathfinder" is a different, larger vehicle; Claude should clarify.

**What would settle it.** Two things:
1. Confirm the 0A pathfinder's mass and power envelope.
2. Decide, on the same acceptance basis as §3.2, whether a subscale flight plus a validated scaling model is acceptable for TRL 6.

### 3.4 Risk class

**Positions:**
- **Claude and Gemini (YAML):** architecture-change.
- **GPT:** project-ending for the selected solar 0B architecture.

All three describe the same causal chain: degraded fallbacks raise delivered $/kg, which may fail the D-02 economics gate. They disagree on how to label it.

**What would settle it.** Run the D-02 economics model with the fallback configuration (~0.3–0.5 MWe tugs, larger fleet, longer trips, reduced site power). If it closes, the risk is architecture-change. If it does not, the risk is project-ending.

### 3.5 Schedule

**Positions:**
- **Gemini:** 4–6 years, needed by 2029.
- **Claude and GPT:** 6–10 years.

The gap follows from §3.2: Gemini's path has no flight step. Gemini's 2029 date has no stated basis, Claude assumes 2031–2034, and GPT leaves the date open.

**What would settle it.** Fix the KDP-0B calendar date, and resolve §3.2.

### 3.6 Sizing distance and resulting area

- **Claude** sizes at the maximum heliocentric distance, bracketed 1.3–1.7 AU. This gives a tug area of ~6,400–27,000 m² (1 AU BOL basis, ~330 W/m²).
- **GPT** uses 0.9–1.3 AU as the stated envelope. It requires sizing at the actual maximum powered distance or explicit derating. At 1.3 AU (~156 W/m² net EOL, assumed factors) this gives a tug area of ~6,400–16,000 m².
- **Site area:** both give ~16,000–51,000 m².
- **Gemini** does not size by distance.

The tug upper-bound difference comes from Claude's 1.7 AU high case. Claude notes that fixing 1.2 AU would cut area by ~2×. GPT notes that 1.3 versus 1.2 AU adds ~17% area.

**What would settle it.** Select the trajectories and fix the maximum powered distance (step 1 for both Claude and GPT).

### 3.7 Scale ratio to heritage

| Model | Ratio | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Gemini | 20–50× | Gateway PPE at ~50 kW/wing |
| GPT | 50–125× (tug); 125–400× (site) | iROSA at 20 kW, required *net EOL* power |
| Claude | ~70–450× (tug) | iROSA per wing, required power converted to *BOL at 1 AU* |

The divergence comes from the choice of heritage baseline and power basis, not from disputed facts. **What would settle it:** agree a common basis (net EOL vs BOL at 1 AU) and decide whether PPE, which Gemini itself describes as "designed for", counts as demonstrated (§4).

### 3.8 Path cost to TRL 6

Summed from each model's own step ranges (GPT notes its packages overlap and are not a priced baseline):

| Model | Total |
|---|---|
| Claude | ~$191M–680M (includes site and supply-chain steps) |
| Gemini | ~$67M–135M |
| GPT | ~$455M–1.7B |

The dominant driver is the TRL 6 step: ground TVAC (Gemini), subscale flight (Claude) or MW flight (GPT). This follows from §3.2–3.3.

### 3.9 Supply chain

Only Claude raises fleet scale (~30–180 MW of 1 AU-BOL array) against space-grade III-V cell output. Claude marks its belief that world output is far below tens of MW/yr as unsure and asks for verification.

**What would settle it.** A manufacturer and industry capacity survey (Claude step 9).

## 4. Evidence register

**Multi-model citations (strongest):**

| Evidence | Cited by | Consistency |
|---|---|---|
| iROSA on ISS, >20 kW/wing (2021–) | Claude (programme confident, power approx.); GPT (confident) | Consistent |
| Psyche, ~21 kW near 1 AU, ~75 m² | Claude (moderately confident); GPT (confident) | Consistent |
| Deep Space 1 SCARLET, ~2.5 kW concentrator | Claude (confident); GPT (confident) | Consistent; both limit it to the concentrator or low-concentration branch |
| ROSA ISS flight experiment (2017) | Claude; GPT | **Conflict.** Claude lists "deployment and retraction, dynamics data". GPT states retraction was unsuccessful and the experiment was jettisoned. *Settle with NASA ROSA experiment reports.* |
| ThrustMe NPT30-I2 iodine EP (2020/2021) | Claude; Gemini | **Conflict in interpretation.** Claude: flight at tens of W, with no array-contamination dataset it knows of. Gemini: iodine–solar-cell interaction "tested in small vacuum chambers". *Settle with Rafalskyi et al. (Nature 2021) and any ThrustMe ground-test reports on cell or coverglass exposure.* |

**Single-model citations (treat as unconfirmed by the panel):**

- **Gateway PPE arrays, ~50 kW/wing (Gemini only).** Gemini's text says "designed for" and "TRL 6-8 for Gateway". Its YAML records "scale_demonstrated: 50 kW", but no flight is cited. This is Gemini's baseline for its 20–50× ratio. *Settle with PPE qualification and flight status documentation.*
- **Claude only:**
  - ISS PVA (power approximate).
  - Lucy UltraFlex latching anomaly (confident).
  - DART ROSA (power unsure).
  - Dawn/Juno/Rosetta (kW unsure).
  - Space Power Facility dimensions.
  - OSAM-1 cancellation and SSPD-1/DOLCE.
- **Claude only, marked unsure (confident: false):** NASA Solar Array Systems MegaFlex/ROSA ground demos (~2012–2015), with tested power and scale unsure.
- **NIEL/DDD arXiv papers (Baur, Campesato et al.).** Claude cites them as TRL 1–3 cell-physics evidence (confident). GPT has not verified their bibliographic details and gives them no system-level credit.

**Flagged errors in the supplied RQ material:**

| Source | Flagged item | Flagged by |
|---|---|---|
| rq-0-22 | III-V cell cost "$100–300/cm²", implying ~$1–3M/m² | Claude |
| rq-0-22 | "~350 W/cm²" concentrator waste heat; Claude computes ~45 W/cm² | Claude |
| rq-0-22 | ISS arrays listed as concentrator heritage | Claude and GPT |
| rq-0-22 vs rq-0-25 | Inconsistent annealing temperatures | Claude |
| rq-0-25 | Annealing data is on GaInAsP, not the baseline cell | Claude; GPT (general form) |
| rq-0-25 | STEREO silicon claim and "0.85–0.90 at 10¹⁰ MeV/g" figure unverified | Claude |
| Supplied review | Routine Earth eclipses at L4/L5 | GPT |
